# Executive and strategy playbooks

Each playbook lists inputs to confirm, the default skill order, when to skip a skill, and what the correction cycle usually fixes. Always follow the core orchestration protocol: plan first, run only what is needed, one correction cycle, one report. Anything meant for a board, investors or the public is a draft for finance and legal review.

## 1. Annual or quarterly strategy

**Confirm first**: the period, the decision horizon, who the strategy is for (leadership team, board), the data available (KPIs, financials, customer insight) and any fixed constraints (budget, headcount, runway).

| Order | Skill | Skip when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | exe-kpi-review | No performance data is provided |
| 2 | exe-strategy-review | Never |
| 3 | exe-competitive-strategy | Competition is not a central question this period |
| 4 | exe-okr-planning | The user wants the strategy only, not goals |
| 5 | exe-plan-review | Never |

**Correction cycle usually fixes**: goals without metrics, options without trade-offs, assumptions presented as facts, more priorities than the team can carry.

**Possible handoffs**: Finance and Accounting (03) to check budget and runway figures; Human Resources (02) for hiring implications.

## 2. OKR setting

**Confirm first**: the period, the level (company, team), the strategy the OKRs serve and the baselines for each metric.

| Order | Skill | Skip when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | exe-okr-planning | Never |
| 2 | exe-plan-review | Never |

**Correction cycle usually fixes**: key results that are tasks instead of outcomes, missing baselines, too many objectives, unclear owners.

## 3. Business case for an initiative

**Confirm first**: the initiative, the decision maker, the approval threshold, cost and benefit estimates the user has, the time horizon and the discount rate or hurdle the company uses (if any).

| Order | Skill | Skip when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | exe-business-case (build mode) | The user already has a case and wants a review only |
| 2 | exe-business-case (review mode) | Never |
| 3 | exe-plan-review | No delivery plan is attached |

**Correction cycle usually fixes**: benefits counted twice, missing ongoing costs, no sensitivity range, no "do nothing" baseline, unlabeled assumptions.

**Possible handoffs**: Finance and Accounting (03) to check the numbers before approval.

## 4. Decision memo

**Confirm first**: the decision, the deadline, who decides, the options already on the table and the criteria that matter most.

| Order | Skill | Skip when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | exe-decision-memo | Never |
| 2 | exe-plan-review (light) | The decision is low stakes and reversible |

**Correction cycle usually fixes**: a recommendation without reasons, missing options, no statement of what would change the decision.

## 5. Board or investor update

**Confirm first**: the audience, the period, the figures available, the format the board expects, and who in finance and legal reviews it.

| Order | Skill | Skip when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | exe-kpi-review | Figures are already summarized and checked by finance |
| 2 | exe-board-update | Never |
| 3 | exe-plan-review | The update contains no plan or forecast claims |

**Correction cycle usually fixes**: figures without a source or comparison, forward-looking statements not flagged, bad news buried, asks of the board not stated.

**Possible handoffs**: Finance and Accounting (03) for figures; Legal, Risk and Compliance (04) for forward-looking statements.

## 6. Monthly business review

**Confirm first**: the period, the data files, the targets and the thresholds the owner uses for "on track".

| Order | Skill | Skip when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | exe-kpi-review | Never |
| 2 | exe-meeting-brief | The user only wants the review, not a meeting agenda |

**Correction cycle usually fixes**: numbers without comparisons, risks without a named record and next step, more than one "one thing".
